correctness.rationale: The original ODE gives v''+beta v'=alpha v^p. Every positive trajectory eventually has v'>0; the exact phase relation (Y²)'=2alpha v^p-2beta Y yields Y~c v^q (q=(p+1)/2>2), hence dv/dt~c v^q and finite-time blow-up. Substitution derives d=-beta/(q+1) and e=beta²q/[2c(q+1)²] in Y=c v^q+d v+e v^{2-q}+R. The proof bounds R by O(v^{3-2q}) for 2<q<3, O(v^-3 log v) for q=3, and O(v^-q) for q>3, each integrable at infinity. Renormalized squared energy has derivative -2beta R, proving finite K and stated tail rates. For q=3, coefficient -3beta³/(16c) of log v was independently verified by SymPy, as were d²+2ce=beta²/(q+1) and the first-order Y coefficient. Comparing two positive phase velocities gives (Y2²-Y1²)'=-2beta(Y2²-Y1²)/(Y1+Y2), so the finite K difference is strictly positive by exact integration.
